options: A datastore that is only accessible to its relevant stakeholders
A datastore that holds only reference data
A datastore, or set of datastores, that is not accessible
A datastore hosted on a remote cloud region
A datastore that has been fully encrypted
questions.explanation: The defining phrase is that a Data Island is a datastore, or datastores, which are not accessible; external integration with them is not possible.

questions.stem: Why has the Data Island largely disappeared?
options: Because organisations no longer store confidential data
Because integration technologies have matured
Because floppy drives were replaced by hard disks
Because data silos replaced them
Because network security concerns have vanished
questions.explanation: Data Islands belong to earlier eras of poor or absent connectivity; as integration technologies matured, datastores stopped being unreachable.

questions.stem: In the era before wireless networking, which of the following was a way data was physically moved between locations, as described in *I Am Datapedia!*?
options: Uploading it to a shared cloud folder
Streaming it through an API
Sending it over a Wi-Fi link
Replicating it with a CDC tool
Carrying floppy drives, big hard disks or even whole desktops
questions.explanation: When datastores could not be connected, small data travelled on floppy drives and large data on big hard disks, and sometimes desktops themselves were moved.

questions.stem: Which reason can lead an organisation to make a datastore a Data Island on purpose?
options: A risk of exposing confidential data to irrelevant stakeholders
A desire to speed up cross-departmental reporting
A need to give every department read access
A plan to build a data warehouse from it
A shortage of database licences
questions.explanation: Where data privacy, security or encryption is lacking and confidential data could reach the wrong people, a datastore is sometimes intentionally isolated as a Data Island.

questions.stem: Which statement about Data Islands and Data Silos is correct?
options: Data Islands and Data Silos are two names for the same thing
Data Silos have disappeared while Data Islands still exist
Data Islands are a modern replacement for Data Silos
Data Islands should not be confused with Data Silos, which still exist
Data Silos are always a subset of a Data Island
questions.explanation: The two terms are distinct: Data Islands have largely disappeared, whereas Data Silos still exist and are treated as a separate topic.

questions.stem: Roughly when does *I Am Datapedia!* say Wi-Fi was 'not a thing', so that only cables connected desktops and laptops to a network?
options: Before 1990
Before 1995
Before 2005
Before 2015
Before 2020
questions.explanation: The author recalls that before 2005 Wi-Fi was not a thing and only cables connected computers to the network.

questions.stem: In which circumstances did datastores come to be regarded as Data Islands?
options: When their data quality was too low to share
When they were used only by one development team
When they were hosted by third-party data companies
When they exceeded a certain storage size
When network security was a big concern or network connectivity did not exist
questions.explanation: In earlier eras, heavy network-security concerns or the absence of network connectivity made external integration impossible, so those datastores were Data Islands.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT given as a reason a Data Island may exist?
options: Lack of a data catalogue
Lack of data security
Lack of data encryption
Absence of network connectivity
Lack of data privacy measures
questions.explanation: Missing privacy, security or encryption, and missing connectivity, are all cited; a missing data catalogue is not mentioned as a cause of Data Islands.

questions.stem: What is the key characteristic that distinguishes a Data Island from other datastores?
options: It stores only unstructured data
It cannot be connected with other datastores
It is always located in a different city
It is owned by the finance department
It is refreshed only once a year
questions.explanation: A Data Island is precisely a datastore that was not connectable with other datastores, whatever its content or location.

questions.stem: How does the author of *I Am Datapedia!* describe modern life without Wi-Fi?
options: Like working on a mainframe
Like living without electricity
Like living in a Data Silo
Like living without air
Like using a floppy drive
questions.explanation: The author jokes that Wi-Fi has become such a norm that living without it is like living without air.
